flags: minor: B's wording (softened translations kept father from responding for himself) previews the answers to R036-05 and R036-09; theme overlap across 01/05/09
R036-01.notes: P5 'for years I had never let him have it' plus the arc of the conference. A contradicts nothing explicit but is unsupported; C reverses the narrator's acceptance of the teacher; D never decided.

flags: minor: key closely paraphrases 'taking the jolts out of every conversation before they reached the other side' (P2), so it's close to a lookup; C is the only real trap
R036-02.notes: Examples soften both directions (father to clerk, pharmacist to father). C wrong: conversations continued, just softened. A/B unsupported.

R036-03.notes: Asking for something already paid for = entitled/owed, blunt; consistent with 'the bill was a theft.' B/C/D are clearly off; D is a literal-minded trap that few will pick.

R036-04.notes: P5: 'It was not the sentence I had been given. It was the sentence I would have wanted to hear.' A/B/D have no support.

flags: minor: R036-06 choice D ('the criticism the narrator expected him to resent') confirms the narrator held an untested expectation, which helps with this item
R036-05.notes: The narrator never let the father hear the real words, yet braced for 'the sharpness I had spent years catching' (P6), so the narrator assumed his reaction without testing it. B: father never asked not to hear; C: not stated; D: unsupported.

flags: minor: overlaps somewhat with R036-05 (both are about the narrator's untested expectation of the father)
R036-06.notes: P7 'Instead he laughed... thank you for telling him straight.' A: no sharp reaction; B: unsupported; C: he says he will talk to Tomas.

flags: minor: the passage shows the father as blunt and demanding but never as interrupting, so the link between the father's manner and Tomas's habits is inferred, not shown; it is still the best choice
R036-07.notes: Laughing in recognition: Tomas's assertive, conversation-owning style mirrors the father's manner (P1, P2). C is a trap built on 'very smart'; A/D unsupported.

R036-08.notes: 'Telling him straight' = directly/honestly; this is a familiar idiom. Fits Ms. Pruitt being 'kind and direct.'

R036-09.notes: The father assumes the narrator has always been 'trying to get it right'; 'otherwise' = that years of translations were softened. B/D unsupported; C is a mild trap but the narrator doesn't disagree that the meeting went well.
